member.name: T:Digifinex.Net.DigifinexAuthenticationProvider
member.summary:
HMAC-SHA256 authentication for the Digifinex REST API.
The signing input is the URL-encoded ASCII-sorted parameter string. For GET requests this is the query string; for POST it is the form-encoded body. When both are present the docs require query & body, query first. The HMAC-SHA256 signature is rendered as lowercase hex and submitted alongside ACCESS-KEY + ACCESS-TIMESTAMP headers. See .

member.name: T:Digifinex.Net.Objects.Sockets.DigifinexAllTickerSubscription
member.summary: Subscription for the Digifinex all_ticker websocket channel (all_ticker.subscribe). Empty params - one subscribe covers every currently listed market. Pushes arrive as all_ticker.update envelopes throttled to ~1Hz server-side; each push carries a partial slice of currently-active tickers and symbols accumulate across pushes.

member.name: T:Digifinex.Net.Objects.Sockets.DigifinexPingQuery
member.summary: Application-level heartbeat for the Digifinex websocket. Sends {"id":N,"method":"server.ping","params":[]}; the server answers with {"error":null,"result":"pong","id":N}. The connection is dropped after 60 seconds of silence, so the periodic registration in fires this query at a sub-60s interval.

member.name: T:Digifinex.Net.Objects.Sockets.DigifinexQuery
member.summary: JSON-RPC subscribe/unsubscribe query for the Digifinex websocket APIs. The server echoes the client-supplied id in both the success ({"error":null,"result":{"status":"success"},"id":N}) and error ({"error":{"code":...,"message":"..."},"result":null,"id":N}) response, so the query is routed back to the originator by id.

member.name: T:Digifinex.Net.Objects.Sockets.DigifinexTickerSubscription
member.summary: Subscription for the Digifinex per-symbol ticker websocket channel (ticker.subscribe). Accepts an explicit list of symbols.

member.name: T:Digifinex.Net.Objects.Sockets.DigifinexTradeSubscription
member.summary: Subscription for the Digifinex public trades websocket channel. A single trades.subscribe call accepts an array of symbols (verified against the live endpoint - the server replies with one success ack and then pushes trades.update frames per symbol). Per-message routing uses the symbol carried in the third params entry so a single subscription serves multiple symbols, each routed to its own handler.
